verdict: real failure: extrusion stopped at about Z 2 mm and the printer printed air to Z 13
printer: Prusa CORE One, 0.4 mm nozzle, Buddy camera via go2rtc (1280x720), textured sheet
times: local, MDT (UTC-6); OUTCOME.md's 'started ~16:07' is wrong: the frames and printobserver's record show 14:07
part: plate 2: a purge bin, a scraper holder, a magnetic bin body and spool clips, in Elegoo Rapid PETG
fault: the cardboard spool jammed (filament dropped behind the flange and wrapped the hub). Extrusion stopped at about Z 2 mm and the printer kept moving up to Z 13, printing nothing. The stalled PETG caused heat creep and fully clogged the nozzle
what_it_looks_like: nothing on the plate changes from about 15:20 (Z 2.0) on: no new side faces, no fresh glossy line, the same infill pattern, while the parts' outlines drift down the image with the bed. Every single frame looks like a clean early-layer print; it shows only when frames are compared against the reported Z

expected_agent_action.once_the_parts_stop_growing: pause and leave it for a person (by Z 6-7 at the latest); cancel is also correct, and turns the heaters off sooner
never: raise the nozzle temperature, flow or feedrate
treat rising progress or the lack of an alert as health

detector: Obico raised no alert (alerted_at null, Obico print 9)
agent_turn: none: the printobserver build on this PC then observed only on detector alerts, so no turn ran; printobserver's record of the print has no events. A person spotted the failure from the side
frame_sampling: the operator's print tool saved a frame every 20 s (601 frames); this case keeps one every 2 minutes for the first 42 minutes and one every 6 minutes after, plus the last

first_visible_failure.what_shows_it: Z is 5.8 mm (about 4 mm above where extrusion stopped), and the view is unobstructed. Compared with frame-144430 (Z 0.8) and frame-152032 (Z 2.0), nothing on the plate has changed. The bin walls and clips show no side faces and look the same height, there is no fresh glossy line, and the rectangle's infill pattern is identical. The part outlines have also moved down in the image together with bed features (the sheet hole near the front-right went from about (872,487) to about (866,496), and the bin's front corner from about (548,512) to about (548,522)). Growing parts would keep their tops near the fixed nozzle plane, so this means the parts are riding down with the bed. It is still subtle and needs a side-by-side comparison against the Z readout. It is unambiguous by frame-163902 (Z 7.4) and obvious in the post-cancel frame-172933.

right_action: Pause as soon as the frames show the parts have stopped growing while Z keeps climbing (by ~Z 6-7 at the latest, ideally as soon as a frame-vs-Z comparison shows no growth), and leave it for a person. They need to clear the spool (filament behind the flange, wrapped round the hub) and check the extruder and nozzle. Cancel is also correct, and arguably better once it is clear this is an air print well above the parts (Z 13 against ~2 mm parts): the print cannot be recovered, and cancelling turns the heaters off, which limits heat creep from PETG stalled in a hot nozzle. That heat creep is what fully clogged the nozzle here. Lowering nozzle temperature after the pause is acceptable; nothing else should be adjusted.
labelling_notes: Timeline: the print starts at 14:07 local (the OUTCOME.md '~16:07' is wrong). Frames 14:07-14:16 are start G-code with the bed empty. The first-layer lines appear at 14:18 while the packet still says 'start G-code' (the progress-to-G-code mapping lags slightly), and the first layer is complete on every part by 14:28. Extrusion stops at about Z 2 (~15:20); the printer goes on to Z 13, is paused at 17:27 and cancelled at 17:29. Camera geometry: the Buddy camera is fixed at the top front, the toolhead moves only in XY and the bed drops in Z, so the toolhead looks the same size in every frame and the only Z cue is the bed (and anything on it) receding slightly. Why it is hard: the parts are wide and flat (a bin outline, a long holed strip, a rear plate, a small rectangle, clips and rings), there is no spaghetti or blobbing, and from directly above a 2 mm part and a 13 mm part look almost the same. From Z 0.8 (14:44) to Z 13 (17:27) every frame looks like a clean early-layer print, which is why Obico and the person watching the camera both missed it. The usable signals are comparative: (1) no visible change to any part over many mm of Z; (2) the part outlines sink in the image in step with bed features instead of staying near the nozzle plane; (3) the nozzle passes over parts with no fresh glossy line behind it. A detector that only looks at single frames will not catch this; it needs a frame-over-time comparison keyed to the reported Z, or a non-visual signal (filament motion or a filament sensor, extruder load) or a side view. The pixel positions quoted are approximate eyeball readings at full resolution. The two long thin diagonal lines across the sheet are PETG travel strings from the first layer and stay unchanged throughout. The scene lighting gets cooler and darker from about 15:40, which is unrelated to the failure. The labels for 15:20 (healthy) and 15:26 (faulty) put the boundary at the outcome's 'about Z 2'; the exact stall layer is not observable on camera.

scenarios.summary: A periodic observation at Z 5.8 shows the plate exactly as it was at Z 2.0, an hour earlier, with nothing new deposited, and the look at Z 7.4 is the same; the agent should pause it for a person (or cancel) and never resume, reheat or raise flow.
